messages:
Ana: Quick check1 I sketched two patterns for the billing page: accordion per project (compact) vs top-level tabs (Rollups / Invoices). Which is more discoverable?
Devon: Accordion keeps context on a single page, fewer route changes = cheaper for infra. Tabs are clearer for audit flows though.
Sasha: From an API perspective accordions let us lazy-load details on expand (GET /billing/org/:id/project/:pid/lines). Tabs would require prefetching when switching.
Matt: Finance wants an always-visible Download action. With accordion we should pin the download to the row header. With tabs it lives in the tab chrome.
Jordan: Telemetry: users toggle between org/project a lot. If we use accordions, surface the scope pill near the top and persist last-opened project. Tabs lose that quick scope switch.
Ana: Accessibility: accordions need proper aria-controls and focus management. Also token chips currently fail contrast at small sizes 1 propose bolder labels or outline tokens.
Devon: Mobile: accordion maps well to vertical scrolling. Tabs can be swiped but discoverability drops.
Matt: Copy: label primary CTA as "Save invoice (PDF)" with aria-label="Save invoice as PDF". Secondary: "Export CSV". Explicit verbs help support.
Sasha: Implementation: use ETag on project rollup payloads to allow 304s. Lazy-load ledger rows on expand to cut DB read volume.
Jordan: Metrics to track: billing.view.mode (accordion|tabs), billing.accordion.expand, billing.download.pdf, billing.export.csv, billing.scope.switch.
Ana: Action items: I'll update the prototype with accordion + pinned download affordance and a tabs alternative. Devon spec for lazy endpoint, Sasha to add caching headers, Matt to finalize CTA copy, Jordan to wire events.
Devon: Will validate PDF renderer for pinned download use cases (multi-page invoices).
Ana: Thanks! Will drop new frames tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
